character_facts: Honorata is capable of maternal feeling but quickly represses it.
Honorata is severe and instructive toward the child.
Aghnar travels with Honorata to the Castaka fortress.
The white-haired boy is almost seven years old and is being trained or judged by warrior standards.
The boy belongs to the Castaka line and is connected to the Metabaron clan through his father.
continuity_links: This page centers on the upbringing and testing of a young Castaka child.
The journey to the Castaka fortress sets up an imminent meeting with the child's father.
dialogue_meaning: A narration box says Honorata momentarily feels maternal weakness and sheds tears.
Honorata mocks the idea of mechanical simulation of female bodily experience and rejects sentimental reflection.
She orders the child to shut himself off from emotion and remember his Castaka identity.
She declares that the child will soon be presented to his father as a worthy warrior of the Metabaron lineage.
A narration box states that at dawn Honorata and Aghnar reach the Castaka fortress riding a trained eodactyl.
locations: the approach to the Castaka fortress
lore_facts: Castaka identity is associated with emotional suppression and warrior discipline.
A child can be formally introduced to his father as a worthy warrior at age seven.
The Metabarons are described as a clan.
The Castaka fortress is a named destination.
An eodactyl is a rideable creature that can be trained for travel.
plot_events: Honorata has a brief emotional reaction while interacting closely with the child.
She suppresses that reaction and returns to a severe, disciplinarian attitude.
Honorata reminds the boy that he is a Castaka.
She tells him that tomorrow he will be seven years old.
She says she intends to introduce him to his father as a warrior who is worthy of the clan of the Metabarons.
At dawn, Honorata and Aghnar travel on a trained eodactyl toward the Castaka fortress.
uncertainties: The page source metadata says p23, but the printed page number visible in the image is 24.
The boy is not explicitly named on this page; identification as Aghnar is uncertain because the final narration says 'Honorata and Aghnar' reached the fortress.
Some narration and speech are stylized and slightly difficult to read precisely, though the main meaning is clear.
visual_summary: A sequence of interior panels shows Honorata briefly overwhelmed with emotion while close to a young white-haired boy in armor, then regaining her harsh composure and addressing him sternly. She tells him that he is a Castaka and announces that on the next day, when he turns seven, she will present him to his father as a worthy warrior of the Metabaron clan. A final wide panel shows Honorata and Aghnar riding a flying eodactyl at dawn toward a tall fortress on the horizon.
